entries.name: header-eof-nested-box-complete-v1-accept#0
entries.description: CONTROL: a COMPLETE size-flagged v1 tree carrying a nested Box constant inline — `sigmaProp(box.value == 1000000)`. It parses and round-trips verbatim, which is what makes the rejects below say something: the shape is legal, and only the missing bytes are not. Without this row the family would just assert that truncated input fails.

entries.name: header-eof-nested-box-complete-v3-accept#1
entries.description: CONTROL: the same complete tree size-flagged at v3. Pairs with the v1 row to show the version plays no part in any of this — the JVM's answer is identical at both.

entries.name: header-eof-ends-at-nested-tree-header-v1-reject#2
entries.description: The input ENDS exactly where the nested Box's own tree header byte belongs: `09` (v1, size-flagged), declared size 2, body = a Box constant (`63`) whose value VLQ is `01`, and then nothing. The nested read is `deserializeErgoTree(r, MaxPropositionSize)`, which overwrites positionLimit with `position + 4096`, so the enclosing declared size does not bound it and the `getByte()` for the nested header runs off the BUFFER — a `BufferUnderflowException`, which is not a ValidationException, so the size bit cannot degrade it. REJECTED. **THE SEPARATING ROW:** an implementation that maps this read error to a soft IO-error kind keeps the tree as `Unparsed` and hands the bytes back, accepting a tree the JVM refuses.

entries.name: header-eof-ends-at-nested-tree-header-v3-reject#3
entries.description: The same input at v3 (`0b`), size-flagged. REJECTED identically — the second half of the pair that shows the degrade gate, not the version, is what decides this. **ALSO A SEPARATING ROW.**

entries.name: header-eof-ends-at-box-value-v1-reject#4
entries.description: CONTROL for the reject side: the input ends one byte earlier, at the Box constant's VALUE rather than at its tree header (declared size 1, body `63`). Also a `BufferUnderflowException` and also REJECTED, and the probe reports that sigma-rust already refuses this one — so a red here would mean something quite different from a red on the two rows above, and a green here is not evidence that they pass.

entries.name: header-eof-truncated-body-v1-reject#5
entries.description: The SECOND failure class. The complete v1 tree's body cut after `d193`, leaving the declared size (50) describing bytes that are not there. The overrun now happens in a VLQ / array read rather than a `getByte()`, so the JVM raises an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead — a DIFFERENT class, equally fatal, equally not a ValidationException. This row exists because the fix shape matters: the correct gate is `anything that is not a ValidationException is hard`, not an enumeration of IO error kinds, and an allow-list that learns `BufferUnderflowException` from the rows above would still get this one wrong.

entries.name: header-eof-truncated-body-v3-reject#6
entries.description: The same truncation at v3. REJECTED identically; the pair pins that neither failure class degrades at either version.
